text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache cardinality spike on inference-runtime-us-west-2 (affecting long-context requests). Paging oncall_jasper and eng_evan. Please acknowledge and triage.

oncall_jasper: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and health dashboards now.

sre_maria: I'm looking at the KV metrics — unique keys spiked by ~12x starting 1778501100, memory pressure on nodes hitting 92%. Continuous-batching queue depth also climbed. Possible correlation with yesterday's alpha longctx rollout (NTK/YaRN sliding window enabled).

eng_evan: confirming: we pushed the sliding-window KV feature to alpha for ~50 customers at 03:00 UTC (NTK=4096, yarn-window=64). Metrics show a big increase in prefix cache entries for longctx requests. Looks like the sliding window is creating many small KV entries instead of reusing prefixes.

prod_ryan: Customer impact? any 5xxs or timeouts reported to support?

cs_ana: Support queue has 7 tickets flagged critical, a couple customers reported elevated latencies for batch chat endpoints. No full outages yet but increased errors on retries for some tenants.

oncall_jasper: reading traces: tail of requests shows repeated cache misses -> regen -> regen -> cache insert thrash. Latency cliff at p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~1.1s. Need a mitigation plan now: reduce cardinality, throttle longctx path, and add KV eviction pressure relief.

sre_maria: Proposed immediate mitigations (can do in order):
1) Disable sliding-window KV feature flag (alpha) -> stops new pathological entries.
2) Flush/Ring-fence KV cache for affected node pools to reclaim memory.
3) Apply runtime throttle: cap continuous batch size and reduce batch window from 20ms -> 5ms.
4) If needed, scale up Dedicated node pool as emergency capacity.

eng_evan: I can flip the feature flag to off for alpha within 60s. Will prepare rollout to avoid global blip (canary across 1 AZ first).

oncall_jasper: Do steps 1 and 3 first. Steps 2/4 if memory stays high. Assigning tasks: evan -> ff toggle, maria -> run cache flush+monitor, jasper -> change batching config and watch traces.

eng_evan: toggling feature flag: `PATCH /flags/alpha/feature-sliding-window {"enabled": false}`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for feature-sliding-window toggle -> canary in us-west-2a

eng_evan: canary success, rolling to remaining alpha tenants. Confirmed patch applied at 1778501312.

sre_maria: observed immediate reduction in new KV key churn after 1778501312. Memory pressure falling but still at ~78% across the pool. Continuous-batch queue depth dropped ~30%.

oncall_jasper: applying continuous batching throttle now: set `CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256` and `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=5` on runtime config for longctx route.

infra-bot: config-update: runtime-config longctx route updated. change recorded at 1778501420.

sre_maria: after throttle: p95 latency improved to ~420ms, p50 ~190ms. Errors on retries dropped by ~60%. KV churn still present but much reduced.

prod_ryan: good. any customer-facing actions? should we notify CS to message affected tenants?

cs_ana: I'll prepare a short message: "We've applied mitigations to reduce elevated latency for long-context endpoints; engineering is monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for fixes." Sending to the 7 customers with tickets now.

eng_evan: we should still do targeted cache eviction/compact for nodes that had the worst churn. maria, can you run a controlled flush on the top 3 nodes (rotate instead of global flush) to avoid cold start spikes?

sre_maria: yes. I'll ring-fence the three highest-heat pods, evict local KV, and then bounce them one at a time: commands below.

sre_maria: ```
# identify top pods
kubectl get pods -l app=inference-runtime --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount | tail -n 3
# run eviction
kubectl exec -it pod/rt-pod-123 -- /opt/runtime/bin/kv-evict --pattern="sliding:*" --force
# restart pod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=rt-pod-123
```

infra-bot: eviction jobs queued on pods: rt-pod-123, rt-pod-119, rt-pod-102

sre_maria: evictions done; pods restarted sequentially. memory on those pods now ~30% reduced. No spike in 5xx during restarts.

oncall_jasper: summary so far: feature flag off, batch throttle applied, targeted evictions + pod restarts. System stabilized but we should keep this incident open while monitoring for 60m and schedule follow-ups.

eng_evan: follow-up action items: 1) fix sliding-window implementation to avoid high-cardinality keys (de-dupe prefixes, increase chunking granularity), 2) add guardrails in runtime to reject extreme NTK requests from alpha by default, 3) add cardinality alarm for KV namespace with auto-throttle.

sre_maria: logging/alerts: raising a new alert rule: KV_unique_keys_rate > 3x baseline for 5m -> pager to sre.

prod_ryan: customer impact note for postmortem: 7 CS tickets, latency increase for 50 alpha tenants, a handful of retries/partial failures. No broad outage. We'll classify as Sev2.

cs_ana: messages sent to affected customers. waiting for replies.

oncall_jasper: can we close the pager now or hold until 1778503234? I'll keep it open until last_message_ts per runbook (monitoring window is 33m). If stable at 1778503234 we'll close and draft postmortem.

incident-bot: Reminder: incident window ends at 1778503234. Please update incident doc with timeline and follow-ups.

sre_maria: adding timeline note: root cause linked to sliding-window kv behavior + NTK setting; mitigation steps executed and validated; follow-ups assigned to eng_evan and eng_platform for hardening.

eng_evan: I'll open a PR with tests that simulate high-cardinality prefix workloads and require performance gates before alpha rollout. ETA EOD.

oncall_jasper: ack. thanks team. I'll start the postmortem draft after the monitoring window closes. leaving thread for any late updates.

cs_ana: FYI — one customer has replied saying latencies back to normal, thanked us. Closing customer updates.

incident-bot: Incident thread will be archived after postmortem is attached. Good job coordinating. :tada:
